hero.subtitle: Mexico's national charrería championship, live at Arena Potosí
hero.description: The Federación Mexicana de Charrería's top event of the year is in San Luis Potosí. This edition honors the legendary charro Andrés "Nito" Aceves.
hero.time: Qualifier days run three sessions: 12:00, 3:30 and 7:00 p.m.
hero.alt: Official poster of the 82nd National Charro Championship San Luis Potosí 2026

items.label: Dates
items.value: October 9 – November 1, 2026 (24 days: 20 of qualifiers, 4 of finals)

items.label: Competitors
items.value: 171 charro teams, 160 escaramuzas and 15 charros completos

items.label: Venue
items.value: Arena Potosí: 10,000 seats, 41 boxes, accessible, 1,000+ parking spaces

items.label: Can't go?
items.value: Live stream on the FMCH Facebook and YouTube channels

tickets.title: Ticket prices
tickets.description: Official prices published by the FMCH. One ticket covers every charreada on the day you choose.
notes: Children under 1.20 m get in free; in numbered seats they sit on your lap.
Prices don't include the ticketing service fees.

items.title: Charreadas by teams
items.description: Teams compete in the classic suertes, from the cala de caballo to the paso de la muerte, and are scored by judges.

items.title: Escaramuzas
items.description: Women's teams riding sidesaddle in synchronized, high-speed routines, wearing traditional dresses.

items.title: Charro completo
items.description: Fifteen riders compete individually across all the suertes for the all-around title.

items.title: Yeguas brutas
items.description: The bronc-riding jineteadero has its own contest, with the final on October 31.

items.title: Pick your session
items.description: Qualifier days have three sessions (12:00, 3:30 and 7:00 p.m.) and the ticket covers all of them.

items.title: Weekdays are cheaper
items.description: Monday to Thursday tickets cost less than Friday to Sunday ones.

items.title: Bring layers
items.description: Late-October evenings in San Luis Potosí cool down quickly.

items.title: Arrive early
items.description: The arena has over 1,000 parking spaces, but weekends draw the biggest crowds.

items.q: When is the National Charro Championship 2026?
items.a: From October 9 to November 1, 2026 at Arena Potosí in San Luis Potosí: 20 days of qualifiers followed by 4 days of finals.
Qualifier days cost $115 MXN (first level) or $290 MXN (VIP general) Monday to Thursday, and $175 or $345 MXN Friday to Sunday. Finals packages (Friday to Sunday) cost $2,300, $5,265 or $5,850 MXN.
Online at masboletos.mx or through the Más Boletos call center at (442) 829 0004.
Children under 1.20 m tall get in free. In numbered seats they don't get their own seat and must sit on an adult's lap.

items.q: Who is the edition dedicated to?
items.a: Andrés "Nito" Aceves, one of the great legends of charrería, honored during his lifetime.
Yes. The FMCH streams the championship live on Facebook and YouTube.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Facts verified on October 19, 2026 against the Federación Mexicana de Charrería website, its Programa General and official ticket-price graphic, and the FMCH release of October 5. The per-session schedule for the final days hasn't been published yet.
